questions.comprehension_passage: Considering two competing firms in a declining industry that cannot support both firms profitably. Each firm has three possible choices as it must decide whether or not to exit the industry immediately, at the end of this quarter, or at the end of the next quarter. If a firm chooses to exit, then its payoff is 0 from the point onward. Every quarter that both firms operate yields each a loss equal to -1, and each quarter that a firm operates alone yields a payoff of 3. For example, if firm 1 plans to exit at the end of this quarter while firm 2 plans to exit at the end of the next quarter then the payoffs are (-1,2) because both firms lose -1 in the first quarter and firm 2 gains 3 in the second. The payoff for each firm is the sum of its quarterly payoffs.
